items.title: Payment for private registry entry offer
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar due date '01.12.2026' for the requested payment, so no period calculation is needed; the date is simply taken as written. Note, however, that the letter itself states this document is only an offer ('Angebot') and that a contract is formed only if and when payment is made ('Mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an; ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande') - so there is no pre-existing legal obligation to pay by this date.

warnings: This is NOT an official invoice and has no connection to the official German land registry (Grundbuch); the letter itself admits this: 'Die Eintragung erfolgt im privaten Verzeichnis des Absenders und steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch.'

The letter explicitly states it is merely an offer ('Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot') and that a contract only comes into existence if you pay; there is no existing debt or legal obligation requiring payment.

This matches a well-known German scam pattern (similar to the 'Gewerbeauskunft-Zentrale' / fake property/business register scams) where private companies send invoice-looking letters to property owners shortly after a purchase or registration, hoping recipients mistake it for an official land registry fee.

Recommendation: do not pay; verify any genuine land registry (Grundbuchamt) matters only through the actual local district court (Amtsgericht) responsible for the property, and consider reporting this letter to the Verbraucherzentrale.
